name: disk
run: for p in / "$HOME/hive-home/honey-store"; do [ -e "$p" ] && df -P "$p" | sed 1d; done | awk '{print} {u=$5; sub("%","",u); if (u+0 > 85) red=1} END {exit red}'
red: exit 1: root or honey over 85% full

name: engine
red: exit 1: a pin is applied on the frame, or the court advertises one for it, and nothing answers on its port; exit 0 says which green: the engine answers, or the frame serves nothing and says so

name: placer
red: exit 1: the placer's last word on the frame is a post it has not cancelled (it wants the frame serving); exit 0: it let the frame go, or never placed it there

name: silent
red: exit 1: the court lists the frame silent (its drone does not reach the court, so no job lands there); the tail is what the court and the tailnet see from outside and what only a person at the machine can check; exit 0: the frame is live

name: downtime
red: exit 1: the drone runs as the user's own unit and the account does not linger, so nothing starts it after a reboot or a logout; exit 3: nothing starts the drone at boot by the shape of its install, and only the keeper mends it (a Mac drone that is a LaunchAgent starts only when he logs in, which FileVault never does unattended: he joins again with sudo, which writes a LaunchDaemon; a systemd unit nobody enabled: systemctl enable hive-drone, as root or as the user); exit 0: it starts by itself; the tail says when this boot began, how the boot before ended (cleanly, or abruptly: power lost), and any memory kills

name: organ
run: found=0; for f in "$HOME"/.hive/organ-*.log; do [ -f "$f" ] || continue; found=1; echo "== $f"; awk '/^== drone started /{n=0; delete b} {b[n++]=$0} END{for(i=0;i<n;i++) print b[i]}' "$f" | tail -n 20; done; [ $found = 1 ] || { echo 'no organ log on this frame'; exit 0; }; for f in "$HOME"/.hive/organ-*.log; do awk '/^== drone started /{n=0; delete b} {b[n++]=$0} END{for(i=0;i<n;i++) print b[i]}' "$f" | tail -n 5 | grep -qiE 'traceback|error|refus' && exit 1; done; exit 0
red: exit 1: an organ's own log ends in an error in the life the drone started last (its last lines are the tail: the import, the port or the probe that failed); exit 0: every organ's current life ends clean, or the frame has none

name: quarantine
red: exit 1: an action that last ran on the frame is quarantined as a repeat crasher; the tail names each by its key, with its command, why, the spine's account of its attempts and whether the frame's drone started again under it; exit 0: nothing the court quarantined last ran there

name: lapses
red: exit 1: the court reads the frame sick (jobs keep lapsing on it, more than it finished since) or holds it; the tail says the hold's case and why, and the jobs the spine says it lost; exit 0: the frame is neither, and takes the fleet's work

name: unheld
red: exit 1: a mind on the frame answered off its schema at its newest tick (fenced, in prose, a verb off its card); the tail names the bee, the rung, the model, the engine and whether its rung said grammar; exit 0: every mind there answers on its schema again

name: ears
red: exit 1: a room on the frame heard speech its ears never transcribed (sayings counted, no final in its ears log), or its station does not answer; the tail is each room's status, hearing session, chunks sent, gate and ears log; exit 0: every room on the frame hears words back, or it has no station

name: mic
red: exit 2: the room's default device will not record a second but a capture card records directly, so the user's audio server holds a stuck source (the audio-server fix answers it); exit 1: nothing is plugged in to record from (every input jack reads off), or no capture card records either: a cable, the card or a mute only the keeper reaches, never the audio-server fix; exit 0: the default records, or the frame has no capture card

name: ray
red: exit 1: the court orders a ray role on the frame and no Ray of that role runs, or a worker runs joined to an address that is not the live head's (a moved head, or one on a silent frame)

name: lastboot
red: exit 1: the frame's previous boot ended without a clean shutdown (no shutdown target or systemd-shutdown near its end): it froze, lost power or was reset; the tail says so first, then the boots listed, the last 30 lines of the boot before and its kernel warnings naming oom, lockup, hung task, mce, watchdog, nvme, I/O error or thermal; exit 0: the boot before shut down cleanly, or no journal here holds it (the tail says which)
